mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines the work done by a constant force on an object?

options.A: The product of the magnitude of the force and the displacement of the object, irrespective of direction.
options.B: The scalar product of the force vector and the displacement vector.
options.C: The change in kinetic energy of the object only when the force is perpendicular to displacement.
options.D: The vector quantity obtained by multiplying force and displacement vectors.

mcqs.answer: The scalar product of the force vector and the displacement vector.
mcqs.explanation: Work is defined as the scalar (dot) product of force and displacement: W = \vec F \cdot \vec s = Fs\cos\theta. This definition includes the magnitude of the force, the magnitude of the displacement, and the cosine of the angle between them, making option B correct. Option A ignores direction, option C misstates the condition, and option D incorrectly calls work a vector.

mcqs.learning_point: Use W = F s cos θ
mcqs.question: A constant force of 10 N acts on an object that moves 5 m making an angle of 60° with the direction of the force. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Work is calculated using W = F s cosθ. Substituting the values: W = 10 N × 5 m × cos60° = 10 × 5 × 0.5 = 25 J. Hence option A is correct. Options B and C result from using incorrect angles or forgetting the cosine factor, and option D would correspond to a perpendicular force (θ = 90°).

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations involves positive work done by the applied force?

options.A: A person pushes a box upward along a vertical wall while the box moves upward.
options.B: A person pushes a crate horizontally to the right while the crate moves left.
options.C: A person holds a weight stationary on a table.
options.D: A person pulls a sled upward while the sled moves downward.

mcqs.answer: A person pushes a box upward along a vertical wall while the box moves upward.
mcqs.explanation: Positive work occurs when the component of the force along the displacement is in the same direction (θ < 90°, cosθ positive). In option A, the force and displacement are both upward, so θ = 0° and work is positive. In B the force and displacement are opposite (negative work), C involves no displacement (zero work), and D also has opposite directions (negative work).

mcqs.question: In which scenario does the applied force do negative work on the object?

options.A: A person lifts a book upward at constant speed.
options.B: A person pushes a car forward and it moves forward.
options.C: A person applies a braking force opposite to the motion of a moving bike, causing it to slow down.
options.D: A person holds a rope stationary while a load hangs from it.

mcqs.answer: A person applies a braking force opposite to the motion of a moving bike, causing it to slow down.
mcqs.explanation: Negative work is done when the force component along the displacement is opposite to the direction of motion (θ > 90°, cosθ negative). In option C, the braking force is opposite to the bike's motion, so the work done by the force is negative. Option A and B have force and displacement in the same direction (positive work), while D involves no displacement (zero work).
